original_question: Let X = (X_1, ..., X_d) have independent components with unit variances, with at most one Gaussian component, and suppose the representation Y_0 = X^T beta_0 is minimal in the sense that there is no proper sub-vector of X whose linear span already represents Y_0. Is the regression parameter beta_0 in unlinked linear regression identifiable up to sign flips and permutations of its components?
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting the paper’s final informal conjecture in Section 5 (Discussion): for ordinary unlinked linear regression with independent, unit-variance components of X, at most one Gaussian component, and a minimal representation, the regression parameter should be weakly identifiable up to sign flips and coordinate permutations. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2507.14986v1))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s core ingredients almost verbatim: independence of the components of X, unit variances, allowance of at most one Gaussian component, the minimality caveat, and the conclusion that identifiability should hold only up to signed permutations rather than in a fully strong sense. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2507.14986v1))
missing_details: State the ULR model explicitly as Y ≍ β0^T X + ε, with ε independent of X; the conjecture in Section 5 relies on the Section 2 setup and is not written as a completely free-standing statement. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/2507.14986))

Add the mild noise hypothesis from Lemma 1: the zero set of the characteristic function φε should contain no open nonempty interval. Under that condition, identifiability in ULR reduces to comparing the laws of β^T X and β0^T X. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2507.14986v1))

Make the ambient space explicit: β, β0 ∈ ℝ^d, and formulate the question in terms of the identifiability set B0 = {β ∈ ℝ^d : β^T X has the same distribution as β0^T X}. Section 2 is organized around this set. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2507.14986v1))

Clarify that the claim is about ordinary single-response ULR, not the multi-response ICA-type model. Section 4.6 proves a signed-permutation identifiability theorem for the multi-response setting and the Section 5 conjecture asks for an analogous statement in ordinary ULR. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2507.14986v1))

Spell out what up to sign flips and permutations means: every alternative β in B0 should satisfy β = DPβ0 for some permutation matrix P and some diagonal sign matrix D with diagonal entries in {−1,1}. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2507.14986v1))

Make the minimality condition fully explicit. The paper states it informally; to make it stand-alone, say that there is no strict subset I ⊊ {1,…,d} and no a ∈ ℝ^|I| such that the same one-dimensional linear form law is already represented by a^T X_I. This is the paper-faithful way to exclude the convolution obstruction discussed in Section 4.3. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2507.14986v1))

If you want the statement to reflect the paper’s exact motivation, note that minimality is needed to remove convolution invariances, while the unit-variance assumption removes scale-family and non-Gaussian stable-law invariances. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2507.14986v1))
refined_question: Consider ordinary single-response unlinked linear regression over ℝ: Y ≍ β0^T X + ε, where ε is independent of X and the zero set of its characteristic function contains no open nonempty interval, so that identifiability is governed by B0 := {β ∈ ℝ^d : β^T X ≍ β0^T X}. Assume X = (X1,…,Xd) has independent components with Var(Xj) = 1 for every j, at most one component Xj is Gaussian, and the representation β0^T X is minimal in the sense that there is no strict subset I ⊊ {1,…,d} and no a ∈ ℝ^|I| such that β0^T X ≍ a^T X_I. Must every β ∈ B0 be of the form β = DPβ0 for some permutation matrix P and some diagonal matrix D with diagonal entries in {−1,1}? ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2507.14986v1))
justification: This is the closest paper-faithful sharpening because your draft matches the concluding open conjecture in Section 5, not the proved d = 2 fourth-moment result in Section 4.5 or the proved multi-response ICA theorem in Section 4.6. The paper’s surrounding discussion shows exactly why the conjecture includes unit variance, minimality, and the signed-permutation ambiguity. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2507.14986v1))
